analysis.file_name: GS Blekos - ## Midterms - First take Europe Strategy Off BS Liabilities Bayer Aramco Gecina Zalando RWE Philips Banks Monitor ## 4 Nov 2026.pdf
analysis.title: Midterms - First take / Europe Strategy / Off BS Liabilities / Bayer / Aramco / Gecina / Zalando / RWE / Philips / Banks Monitor
key_insights: GS raises STOXX 600 EPS growth forecasts to 18% for 2026 and 7% for 2027, and introduces a 2028 forecast of 5%, with strong contributions from Financials and Commodities.

GS economists expect nominal Euro-area GDP growth of 3.3% in 2026 and 2.8% in 2027, well below the pace of European earnings growth. GS attributes the gap to the sector composition and global exposure of the listed market.

Hyperscaler free cash flow has turned negative and debt issuance has accelerated. Hyperscalers have issued $271B of debt year to date, above GS's full-year 2026 forecast of $250B, with more than $40B of deals announced since October 29.
Some of the hyperscaler issuance is a pull-forward of planned 2027 supply. GS sees scope for more, but expects capital markets access to be uneven across issuers and dependent on market tone.
GS estimates $657B of year-to-date global AI-related debt issuance across syndicated credit markets through November 2, a much larger scope than the five hyperscalers alone.

Bayer: GS remains Buy, citing a potentially imminent court ruling on the glyphosate settlement and strong Pharma performance. GS raises Nubeqa forecasts and lifts its 12m price target 4% to €66.0 from €63.5.
Bayer: GS expects Crop to remain volatile near term and sees the Pharma growth phase as under-appreciated by the market.
Saudi Aramco: GS is Buy after a 3Q26 net income beat and strong cash flow generation. The stock trades at a 12% discount to its 5Y average P/E, and the SAR34 12m price target implies c.30% upside.
Aramco: GS changes EPS estimates by +0.4%/+0.0%/+0.0% for 2026/27/28 after incorporating 3Q26 results.

Gecina: GS downgrades to Neutral from Buy because pipeline lettings are slower than expected. 2026-30E EPS estimates change by -8% to 0%, with longer lead times to let pipeline projects, slightly lower rental reversion and no share buyback assumed.

Gecina: GS 2027E/28E EPS sits c.3%/4% below Visible Alpha consensus, with a 1% 4-year EPS CAGR and 27E/26E EPS -4% reflecting company guidance of 2027 as a transition year. The 12m PT falls c.10% to €72.6 from €80.4.
Zalando: GMV growth improved sequentially, supported by third-party and ZMS, and the Zalando Extended announcement is an incremental positive. TP remains €44.
RWE: a gas plants auction brings upside to GS's base case.
Philips: strong Q3 orders and resilient margins, with Diagnosis & Treatment growth seen as the next key unlock.
The note also links a US midterm elections first take dated 4 Nov 2026 and a European banks deposit and lending volume and pricing monitor for September 2026. The text gives no detail on either.
